newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to issue three-year bonds, no date set.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to issue three-year bonds, no date set.

text.p: Ukraine plans to sell one billion hryvnia of three-year fixed-rate interest-bearing government bonds, the government press service said on Tuesday.
A statement did not say when sales of the OVDZ bonds, with a nominal value of 100 hryvnias each, would begin.
It said the bonds would pay annual interest of 15 percent in year one, followed by nine percent in each of the second and third years.

Ukraine's Finance Ministry has regularly sold three-, six-, nine- and 12-month discount T-bills on the two-year-old government securities market, on which foreign participation is estimated at 70 to 80 percent.
The draft 1997 budget forecasts annual inflation at 24 to 25 percent this year, although Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said last month it would be no higher than 15 to 16 percent.
Yields on sales of T-bills last week stood at 20.13 percent for six-month paper, 28.13 percent on nine-month paper and 30.46 for one-year bills.
The ministry tried selling 18-month Treasury bills in April but none were bought.
